newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on CBOT collapse, rainfall.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on CBOT collapse, rainfall.

text.p: A collapse in the Chicago markets plus forecasts for rain in the dry wheat areas of western Kansas pressed KCBT hard red winter wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.

"Chicago led the way down and the storm system should track right through the heart of the driest areas of Kansas and Nebraska," a trader said. "Plus we're only two weeks away from harvest so the pressure is on."
USDA Monday said as of Sunday, the U.S. winter wheat crop was 50 percent good to excellent, below the 53 percent in that category the previous week.
But traders said that satisfactory production prospects remained and the showers forecast for Kansas should boost the crop outlook there.
Meteorologists said rain was likely in western Kansas over the next five days.
The May contract expired at 1201 CDT down 6-1/2 cents at $4.61-1/2 a bushel.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with new crop July down 14-1/4 cents at $3.80-1/2 a bushel.
KCBT wheat futures volume was estimated by the KCBT at 38.605 million bushels, above the 33.275 million traded Monday.
